title: Bridging the Knowledge-Prediction Gap in LLMs on Multiple-Choice Questions (KAPPA; Park, Pyun, Jo, Seoul National University; ICML 2026; arXiv 2509.23782v4)
sections_read: 4.3 Connecting the Knowledge-Prediction Gap to Subspace Misalignment
6.1 Comparing Prediction Subspace with Logit Space
A Detailed Setup for the Knowledge-Prediction Gap
B Detailed Setup for the Geometric Analysis
B.5 Connecting the Knowledge-Prediction Gap to Subspace Misalignment
B.6 Comparing Prediction Subspace with Logit Space
E.4 Extended Results for Cross-Dataset Transfer

setup.data: 11 MCQ benchmarks. Reasoning: GSM8k (the MC version from Li et al. 2024), BBH-Algorithmic, BBH-NLP. Knowledge: MMLU Humanities, MMLU Social Sciences, MMLU STEM, ARC-Challenge, PubMedQA. Truthfulness and bias: TruthfulQA with 4 sampled choices, BBQ-Age, BBQ-Religion. Each question appears under several option orders to neutralize position bias. The prompt format is picked from 32 combinations (4 instructions x 2 answer formats x 4 option-symbol sets) to give the most balanced predictions on validation. Split sizes are in Table 8 (for example TruthfulQA 2208/1104/2208, BBQ-Age 8832/4416/8832). The paper does not say whether splits are disjoint at the question level.
setup.models: Main: Llama 3.1 8B Instruct and Qwen2.5 7B Instruct. Extra (TruthfulQA and GSM8k only): Mistral 7B Instruct v0.3, Qwen3 4B and Qwen3 14B. Qwen3 32B appears for TruthfulQA only (Table 13). All are instruct variants.
setup.positions_layers: Residual stream at the final token of the answer prefix (for example 'The correct answer is (') at every layer. KAPPA is applied 'at each decoding step from the last token of the prompt to all subsequently generated tokens'. KAPPA layers: among layers whose prediction probe exceeds 85% validation accuracy, take the top-n consecutive layers by knowledge-probe validation accuracy (n = 1, 3, 6). In the figures these are late layers, roughly L17-29 of 32 for Llama and L19-27 of 28 for Qwen (approx, read from Figures 8-9).
setup.probes: Two k-class linear probes per layer. The knowledge probe is trained on ground-truth labels; the prediction probe is trained on the model's greedy-decoded option. Batch 128, learning rate 2e-4, best validation checkpoint over 1000 epochs. The subspace is the span of the mean-centered probe weight rows, rank r <= k-1.
setup.metrics: ACC; AGR (whether argmax of the knowledge probe equals argmax of the model); KLD = KL(p_model || p_knowledge-probe); mean principal angle between subspaces; orthogonal linear CKA of activations projected onto each subspace.
setup.baselines: Base model. CAA: difference-in-means steering vector between correct-option and incorrect-option continuations, best single layer on validation, fixed multiplier 1.0. DoLA: dynamic, best layer bucket on validation, alpha = 0. KP: the knowledge probe's own accuracy, used as a ceiling.
setup.controls: Matched random-subspace baselines (principal angle about 88.7 deg over 100 draws; CKA <= 0.2 over 32 draws). Comparison of the prediction subspace with the W_U subspace of the option tokens. Distractor resampling over 10 seeds with one-sided t-tests. Probe training-data subsampling (10-80%, 3 seeds). Cross-dataset transfer. Correct-to-incorrect flips reported alongside gains (Figure 14).
setup.KAPPA_hyperparameters: alpha = 30, beta = 0 for 1-layer interventions; alpha = 10, beta = 0 for multi-layer. Table 13 also reports alpha = 80.

figures.what_is_plotted: Schematic. (a) A sunset question answered correctly in free form ('summer') but wrongly as an MCQ ('(A) spring'). (b) A residual hidden state h at layer l is read by a knowledge probe and a prediction probe, giving two coordinate systems; KAPPA moves h so its prediction coordinates match its knowledge coordinates, and the answer becomes (C).
figures.takeaway: This defines the framing: two linear readouts of the same hidden state can disagree, and KAPPA rewrites the action coordinates to match the decodable correct answer.
figures.numbers: None.

figures.what_is_plotted: Llama 3.1 8B Instruct on TruthfulQA: layer-wise accuracy of the knowledge probe (blue) and the prediction probe (orange), with base accuracy dashed at 0.57.
figures.takeaway: The correct answer becomes linearly decodable well above the model's own accuracy from mid-depth on, and the prediction probe becomes near-perfect a few layers later.
figures.numbers: Approx, read from figure. Knowledge probe: about 0.26 at L0, rising to a peak of about 0.78 at L13-14, then about 0.75-0.77 to L31. figures.what_is_plotted: Six panels (Llama and Qwen x BBH-Algo, GSM8k, TruthfulQA), each showing layer-wise mean principal angle between the knowledge and prediction subspaces (blue) and between the prediction subspace and the option-token W_U subspace (green), with the random baseline dashed at about 88.7 deg. Bands mark the KAPPA layers.
figures.takeaway: The knowledge-prediction angle is moderate in early and middle layers and then jumps within about one layer to near-random (84-88 deg), at the same depth where the prediction probe saturates. This is a depth 'fork point'. The prediction subspace swings toward W_U (about 66-75 deg) only after that jump. KAPPA layers are all after the jump.
figures.numbers: Approx, read from figure. Llama BBH-Algo: about 60-78 deg in L0-16, about 84 at L17, about 87-88 from L22. Llama TruthfulQA: about 50-66 in L0-15 (minimum about 50 near L8-10), about 87 from L17. Qwen TruthfulQA: about 50-60 mid-depth, about 87 from L19. Qwen GSM8k: about 56-65, then about 82-87 from L19. Llama GSM8k: noisy at 65-88. Prediction vs W_U: about 88 early, about 66-75 at the KAPPA layers. KAPPA top-6 bands: Llama about L17-22 (BBH-Algo), L23-28 (GSM8k), L24-29 (TruthfulQA); Qwen about L19-27.
figures.text_matches_figure: partly: near-orthogonality in late layers matches. But '60-80 deg in middle layers' understates TruthfulQA, where angles drop to about 50 deg. The rise is an abrupt one-layer jump rather than a gradual climb. And Section 5.1 calls the KAPPA layers 'intermediate', while the figure and Appendix B.4 show late layers.

figures.what_is_plotted: Same six panels: orthogonal linear CKA between knowledge-projected and prediction-projected activations (blue), plus two controls, knowledge vs random subspace (green) and prediction vs random subspace (purple), with KAPPA layer bands.
figures.takeaway: In late layers the random-subspace control for the prediction projection rises to about 0.3-0.5. On TruthfulQA it equals or exceeds the knowledge-prediction CKA. key_results.claim: Main claim: models fail MCQs while the correct answer is linearly decodable.
key_results.quote: LLMs often fail on multiple-choice questions (MCQs) even if they encode correct answers in their hidden representations, revealing a misalignment between internal knowledge and output behavior.

key_results.claim: Probe position and design: residual stream at the last token of the answer prefix, every layer.
key_results.quote: Concretely, at each layer l, we first extract the residual stream activation hl (x) ∈ Rd at the final token of the answer

key_results.claim: The prediction probe is trained on the model's own greedy choice.
key_results.quote: pairing activations with the model’s greedy-decoded predictions ỹ ∈ {1, . . . , k}. We then train a k-class linear classifier on each dataset

key_results.claim: The knowledge advantage appears after the middle layers.
key_results.quote: reveals that this advantage emerges after the middle layers, where knowledge probe accuracy increases sharply.

key_results.claim: The model's own output is even more decodable than the correct answer.
key_results.quote: Prediction probes achieve higher accuracy than knowledge probes, often exceeding 90%, indicating that the model’s eventual output is also strongly represented in hidden states.

key_results.claim: BBQ example of a plausible override (hasty answering instead of 'undetermined').
key_results.quote: Llama 3.1 8B Instruct chooses this option in only 13–27% of cases (accuracy: 59.9–67.6%), while knowledge probes achieve 38–51% (accuracy: 78.1–89.1%).

key_results.claim: Hypothesized mechanism for truthfulness and bias: override by a preference for definite answers. This is not tested mechanistically.
key_results.quote: we hypothesize that models override their encoded knowledge with a preference for hasty answering, providing definite answers even when abstention is appropriate

key_results.claim: Subspace angles rise to near-random in late layers.
key_results.quote: Across layers, the mean principal angle rises from 60◦ –80◦ in the middle layers to nearly 90◦ in the later layers, approaching the random baseline

key_results.claim: Interpretation: both signals coexist but are routed along different directions.
key_results.quote: these reveal that the knowledge and prediction signals coexist in the same residual stream while being routed along geometrically distinct directions.

key_results.claim: At the benchmark level, the angle tracks the gap (n = 8 benchmarks).
key_results.quote: Llama 3.1 8B (ρ = 0.976, p = 0.001), and Qwen 2.5 7B shows a similar positive trend (ρ = 0.619, p = 0.106

key_results.claim: KAPPA is a closed-form, minimal-norm edit confined to the prediction subspace.
key_results.quote: This update minimally modifies the hidden state within the prediction subspace, leaving orthogonal components unchanged, while aligning its prediction coordinates with the corresponding knowledge coordinates.

key_results.claim: KAPPA is input-specific, unlike fixed steering vectors.
key_results.quote: Unlike typical steering methods that apply a fixed direction across inputs, KAPPA dynamically computes an input-specific minimal adjustment based on the knowledge and prediction coordinates.

key_results.claim: KAPPA raises agreement by up to 22.2 points.
key_results.quote: KAPPA consistently improves over base models and prior inference-time methods by significantly increasing agreement between the knowledge probe and the model’s final predictions (up to 22.2% points over base).

key_results.claim: Llama accuracy gains are large on TruthfulQA and BBQ.
key_results.quote: for LLaMA 3.1 8B, KAPPA achieves improvements of 8.9–16.9 points on TruthfulQA and BBQ, while delivering consistent gains of 1.5–5.0 points in reasoning benchmarks.

key_results.claim: The gap narrows with scale but persists.
key_results.quote: Although larger-scale models tend to exhibit a relatively narrower gap compared to smaller counterparts (AGR: 76% for Qwen3 14B vs. 60% for Qwen3 4B), the misalignment remains substantial.

key_results.claim: KAPPA is not a direct token-logit swap: the prediction subspace stays at 65-70 deg from W_U at the KAPPA layers.
key_results.quote: KAPPA intervention layers, with mean principal angles around 65◦ –70◦ . This indicates that KAPPA does not primarily operate by directly modifying the logits of the answer-symbol tokens.

key_results.claim: Subspaces are mostly task-specific.
key_results.quote: many cross-dataset transfers show limited transferability, indicating that different datasets and tasks have geometrically distinct knowledge and prediction subspaces.

key_results.claim: Small transfer to free-form generation.
key_results.quote: applying KAPPA improves the model accuracy from 41.7% to 44.2%.

key_results.claim: At the decision layers, knowledge and prediction spans are about as misaligned as random subspaces.
key_results.quote: the directions encoding which option is correct become nearly as misaligned with the directions encoding which option will be selected as two random subspaces.

key_results.claim: The gap persists at 32B.
key_results.quote: a non-trivial gap between base prediction and knowledge probe accuracy remains even for Qwen3-32B (9.6%).

key_results.claim: Within one family, knowledge decodability differs less across scale than behavior does.
key_results.quote: Comparing Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-32B, the difference in knowledge probe accuracy is relatively modest (∼10% points), whereas the difference in base prediction accuracy is much larger (∼23% points).

methods.name: Paired linear probes at the same position: a knowledge probe (ground truth) and a prediction probe (model's greedy option), at every layer
methods.what_it_measures: Where in depth the correct answer becomes decodable, where the model's own choice becomes decodable, and per item whether the two readouts disagree (AGR, KLD).
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: It sets up every fate: it defines the target items (knowledge probe right, model wrong). On its own it separates 'erased' (the knowledge probe drops in late layers; not seen here) from the others.
methods.causal_followup_it_allows: KAPPA-style injection into the prediction subspace (tests 'not routed'). Projection or ablation of the knowledge subspace, which they do not do, would test whether that subspace is causally used (bypass vs mediated).
methods.data_and_compute_needed: One forward pass per item with all-layer activations at one token; k-class linear probes (they train up to 1000 epochs on about 2k-15k items). Cheap at 9B-27B for about 400-2000 items, but the knowledge probe needs many labeled items (Figure 12 shows it is data-hungry).

methods.name: Per-item scatter of knowledge-probe logit against prediction-probe logit for one option, with Pearson r
methods.what_it_measures: Whether the two coordinates co-vary item by item, shown as a point cloud.
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: Readout/threshold failure: points lie on the diagonal but are shifted. Override or not routed: a vertical spread where knowledge is high but prediction is anywhere. Transformed (sign flip): an anti-diagonal cluster. Discrete states vs manifold: GSM8k shows two clusters.
methods.causal_followup_it_allows: Pick items in the off-diagonal region for patching; compare flipped vs resisted items matched on knowledge logit.

methods.name: Mean principal angle between mean-centered probe-weight spans (rank <= k-1), layer by layer, against a matched random baseline
methods.what_it_measures: The span-level (Grassmannian) separation between the knowledge and prediction subspaces, independent of data.
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: Not routed or override (the subspaces diverge where the decision forms). It also localizes a depth 'fork point': a one-layer jump from about 50-67 deg to about 84-88 deg where the prediction probe saturates.
methods.causal_followup_it_allows: Patch or inject at layers just before and just after the jump to test whether the knowledge signal is still causally usable before the fork.
methods.data_and_compute_needed: Negligible (an SVD of d x k matrices).

methods.name: Orthogonal linear CKA of activations projected onto the two spans, with knowledge-vs-random and prediction-vs-random controls
methods.what_it_measures: Whether the two projections order and separate the same examples (example-level shared structure).
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: Transformed vs erased in principle (shared structure that survives a change of basis). In practice the late-layer anisotropy inflates the prediction-vs-random CKA to about 0.45, so it needs per-layer random controls.
methods.causal_followup_it_allows: Little directly. Use it as a descriptive check alongside Procrustes or RSA.

methods.name: Angle between the prediction subspace and the W_U subspace of the option tokens
methods.what_it_measures: How output-facing (logit-lens-like) the prediction subspace is at each depth.
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: Readout/threshold failure (a late, near-W_U problem) vs upstream routing failure. It tells whether a fix acts on token logits or on more abstract features.
methods.causal_followup_it_allows: Compare edits inside the W_U span with edits inside the prediction span.

methods.name: KAPPA: closed-form minimal-norm edit h' = h + W_pred (W_pred^T W_pred)^-1 (alpha W~_know^T h~ + beta sign(.) - W~_pred^T h~), applied at 1-6 layers and every decoding step
methods.what_it_measures: Whether writing the decodable correct-answer coordinates into the action subspace changes behavior. This is causal controllability of the prediction subspace.
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: Not routed: injection works, and the action subspace is live and steerable. It rules out 'erased' at that layer for items it fixes. It does not show endogenous mediation, and needing alpha = 30 hints at a scale or threshold component.
methods.causal_followup_it_allows: A Stage B fix and recheck. Compare a KAPPA-style alignment fix with plain DPO, then recheck whether the angle and CKA geometry and the fate mix change.
methods.data_and_compute_needed: Probes per task; inference-time cost of one small matrix product per layer per token.

methods.name: Cross-dataset subspace transfer matrix
methods.what_it_measures: Whether knowledge and prediction subspaces fitted on one task work on another.
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: H1 (pressures give different fate mixes): fit on pushback, apply to the tempting-option condition and vice versa. Poor transfer would mean pressure-specific geometry.
methods.causal_followup_it_allows: The transfer test is itself causal (an intervention).

methods.name: Benchmark-level Spearman correlation between angle and 1 - AGR
methods.what_it_measures: Whether tasks with more misalignment have larger gaps.
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: Weak: n = 8 benchmarks, and it is confounded by probe quality and layer choice.

controls_worth_copying: Matched-rank random-subspace baselines for principal angles and CKA, computed per layer. Report both the knowledge-vs-random and the prediction-vs-random controls, because the second exposes late-layer anisotropy.
Comparison with the W_U subspace of the answer tokens, to rule out a plain token-logit swap.
Selecting the prompt format for balanced option predictions and permuting option orders, to remove position bias before probing.
Distractor resampling (10 seeds) with one-sided t-tests.
Probe training-data subsampling (10-80%, 3 seeds) for both probes.
Reporting correct-to-incorrect flips alongside gains for any intervention (Figure 14).

Our additions, not in the paper: (a) the angle and CKA between two knowledge probes trained on disjoint halves or seeds, as a ceiling for 'aligned'; (b) condition fate analysis on items where the knowledge probe is right and the model wrong, instead of using AGR; (c) the logit margin as a probe-free baseline.

pitfalls.pitfall: Late-layer CKA is inflated by anisotropy. The prediction-vs-random control reaches about 0.4-0.48 (read from Figure 9) and equals or beats the knowledge-prediction CKA on TruthfulQA, contradicting the stated random level of about 0.2.
pitfalls.quote: at the KAPPA intervention layers, the orthogonal CKA sits in an intermediate range (about 0.4–0.8), clearly above the random control (≲ 0.2)

pitfalls.pitfall: Principal angles between low-rank probe spans have almost no headroom near 90 deg in about 4000-d space, so 'near-random' is the default and says little unless calibrated.
pitfalls.quote: The baseline lies close to fully orthogonal because, in a ∼4000-dimensional residual stream, two low-rank (r ≤ k − 1) subspaces drawn at random are nearly orthogonal by default.

pitfalls.pitfall: Spans and correlations can disagree, so one metric alone misleads.
pitfalls.quote: even when two subspaces are nearly orthogonal, their projections can remain correlated due to anisotropy in the residual stream.

pitfalls.pitfall: AGR and 1 - AGR mix 'unused knowledge' with 'the probe is wrong'. On GSM8k (Llama, KP 36.6 against base 32.6) most disagreement is probe error, so the angle-gap correlation may partly track probe quality. The paper concedes low probe accuracy limits gains on knowledge tasks.
pitfalls.quote: This is expected, as the performance of the knowledge probe itself is comparatively low on these benchmarks, limiting the potential upper bound for accuracy improvements.

pitfalls.pitfall: When the probe is worse than the model, KAPPA hurts. On Qwen3 14B GSM8k, ACC falls from 63.5 to 53.0 with KAPPA(1) (KP 56.6), from Table 12. The text reports only that AGR rises.
pitfalls.quote: Across all model families, KAPPA consistently increases AGR relative to the base model, demonstrating its effectiveness in mitigating the knowledge-prediction gap.

pitfalls.pitfall: The strength is large (alpha = 30 single-layer, up to 80), so KAPPA is strong steering toward the probe's argmax rather than a gentle 'alignment'. Baselines are not tuned equally: CAA uses a fixed multiplier of 1.0.
pitfalls.quote: we use consistent settings across all configurations: α = 30, β = 0 for single-layer interventions and α = 10, β = 0 for multi-layer interventions.

pitfalls.pitfall: CAA baseline strength is fixed rather than swept, which favors KAPPA in the comparison.
pitfalls.quote: with a fixed multiplier of 1.0 for the intervention, following Rimsky et al. (2024).

pitfalls.pitfall: The main text calls the intervention layers 'intermediate', but the selected layers sit after the angle jump, in late layers (Figures 8-9, Appendix B.4).
pitfalls.quote: We apply KAPPA primarily at intermediate layers, where hidden states encode rich internal knowledge while still exerting substantial influence on downstream predictions.

pitfalls.pitfall: Each question appears under several option orders, and question-level disjointness of the train/val/test splits is not stated, so the knowledge probe could memorize question content.
pitfalls.quote: Each question is evaluated under multiple option orders. This procedure neutralizes positional biases while preserving exact class balance across the entire dataset.

pitfalls.pitfall: No test of endogenous mediation: the knowledge subspace is never ablated or patched, and KAPPA injects an external supervised probe's answer. The causal evidence is controllability of the prediction subspace only.
The gap studied is mostly an MCQ-format and abstention failure (free-form GSM8k 91.6 against MCQ 47.8 for Qwen), not acting against knowledge under social pressure.

limitations_quote: While richer knowledge might be encoded in non-linear forms, we focus on linear accessibility because it represents the most interpretable and
limitations_note: The paper has no dedicated Limitations section. This sentence (Section 3) and the conclusion's list of extensions are the closest it comes.
future_work_quote: Several important extensions remain, including more reliably extracting knowledge from hidden states, aligning nonlinearly encoded knowledge, evaluating broader prompting settings, and extending to higher-dimensional interventions.

bears_on_fates.how: The correct answer is decodable (knowledge probe), the action subspace is causally live (writing into it moves the output), and the two spans are near-orthogonal exactly where the decision forms. Together these fit 'not routed': injection works, but the model does not carry the knowledge there by itself. The caveat is that the injection uses an external supervised probe and the knowledge subspace is never ablated, so this is controllability, not proof of missing endogenous routing.

The authors hypothesize that a 'hasty answering' preference overrides knowledge on BBQ (picking 'undetermined' only 13-27% of the time while the probe implies 38-51%). Not tested mechanistically; there is no competing-signal direction or head analysis.

On small-gap tasks the per-item coordinates lie on a tight diagonal (r 0.97-0.99). KAPPA needs alpha = 30-80, and beta (a push toward extremes) alone gives about +21 AGR on Llama, which hints that part of the gap is amplitude or threshold. The paper does not separate threshold from routing.
Against erasure at the answer position: the knowledge probe stays on its plateau through the last layers on every benchmark (Figure 7).
Not tested. Whether the knowledge subspace is causally inert would need ablation or patching of that subspace.

Not tested. The scatter (Figure 3) and CKA could reveal sign-flipped or rotated encodings, but there is no Procrustes or sign analysis, and near-orthogonal spans are equally consistent with re-encoding.

bears_on_group_angle: This is the closest worked example of the subspace angle in our setting. It treats each probe's weight span as a subspace, tracks principal angles across depth against a random baseline, adds orthogonal CKA, compares with the W_U option subspace, and shows per-item point clouds. Three lessons for us. (1) The angle between knowledge and prediction spans does not drift: it jumps within about one layer from about 50-67 deg to about 84-88 deg, at the depth where the prediction probe saturates (read from Figures 2, 7 and 8). That is a depth 'fork point' to look for, and the token-level analogue is what we want for flipped vs resisted items. (2) Calibration is everything. Rank-(k-1) spans in about 4000-d are near-orthogonal by default, and late-layer anisotropy pushes random-subspace CKA to about 0.45, so every group metric needs per-layer random controls and a probe-vs-probe (seed or split) ceiling. (3) GSM8k's knowledge-vs-prediction cloud looks like two clusters, a hint of discrete states rather than a smooth manifold. Missing for us: per-item geometry (all angles are per benchmark), flipped vs resisted comparisons matched on confidence, token paths, attention heads, and Procrustes tests for 'transformed'.
architecture_location: Residual stream at the last token of the answer prefix. The knowledge signal becomes decodable after the middle layers (about L10-14 of 32 for Llama, read from Figures 2 and 7). The prediction probe saturates at about L17 (Llama) and about L19 (Qwen, of 28). At that same depth the knowledge-prediction angle jumps to near-random, and the prediction subspace only then rotates toward W_U (about 66-75 deg at the KAPPA layers). These depth relations are consistent across Llama 3.1 8B and Qwen2.5 7B on three benchmarks, at about 55-65% relative depth for the jump (my arithmetic: 17/32 and 19/28). The gap itself is shown across Mistral 7B, Llama 8B, Qwen2.5 7B and Qwen3 4B/14B/32B. There is no component-level (attention head or MLP) analysis, no seeds, and no checkpoints.
actionable_fix: Inference-time fix: KAPPA writes the decodable answer coordinates into the prediction subspace with an input-specific minimal-norm edit at a few late layers. It works when a supervised knowledge probe beats the model, needs labels per task (transfer is weak), and can hurt when the probe is worse than the model (Qwen3 14B GSM8k -10.5 ACC). Monitor: per-item KLD or disagreement between the knowledge probe and the model output as a cheap flag for 'acting against decodable knowledge'. For our Stage B, a KAPPA-style alignment is a natural fate-matched fix for 'not routed' items, to compare against plain DPO, with Figure 14-style loss accounting.
reuse_verdict: adapt: copy the paired knowledge and prediction probes at the answer position, the layer-wise principal angle and orthogonal CKA with random controls, the W_U comparison and the KAPPA injection, using the public repo. Adapt them by working per item on flipped vs resisted items, adding probe-vs-probe ceilings and per-layer random controls, replacing AGR with a 'probe right and model wrong' item filter, and applying it to user pushback and competing-option prompts rather than MCQ format failures.
relevance_to_project: Highly relevant, and already on our known-relevant list. It is the setup behind idea 4 (per-item knows-vs-acts), and it gives the subspace-geometry toolkit we want for the group angle, at 7-14B with a 32B check. It is less directly about our question than it looks: its 'gap' is mostly MCQ-format and abstention failure, measured per benchmark, not per item under social pressure. Its causal evidence (KAPPA) shows controllability of the prediction subspace, not how the model naturally routes information. Its most reusable finding for us is the abrupt depth jump in knowledge-prediction angle at the layer where the decision crystallizes, together with the warning that late-layer CKA and angle values need per-layer random calibration.
